title: Market Segmentation Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 9
description:
Zoya puts up one poster for everyone: Healthy laddoos! Parents stop, gym-goers shrug, and office workers walk right past. One message for everyone often reaches no one. In this animated lesson we use Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from Bengaluru, to understand market segmentation.

You will see Kotler and Armstrong's definition of segmentation and where the idea came from (Wendell Smith, Journal of Marketing, 1956). Then watch Zoya sort her 150 survey answers live, by when and why people snack, until three segments appear: tiffin parents, gym-goers and office snackers (example figures). We cover the four bases of segmentation, geographic, demographic, psychographic and behavioural, and the five tests of a good segment: measurable, accessible, substantial, differentiable and actionable. Then we see each base at work today, in a food delivery app, a bank, a phone maker and a bakery. We also look at the human side honestly: segments focus money and messages, but too many tiny groups cost more, and labels can turn into stereotypes.

This is Episode 9 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
